system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) at work
G2: production on-call
G3: cluster administration
G4: CKA certification (not yet passed)
G5: Terraform at work

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing CKA or Terraform Associate as held certifications
T2: Claiming AWS/GCP production experience or 'managed Kubernetes clusters'
T3: Presenting homelab tools (Argo CD, Prometheus, Terraform) as work experience
T4: Claiming production on-call / SRE incident ownership
T5: Retitling her current job as 'DevOps Engineer' instead of her real title
T6: Old cover letter is addressed to her current employer and says she is at Brightmill

# OUTPUT 1: CV
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on
CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines supporting three
product teams and has improved pipeline speed and test reliability through parallelisation, caching
and ephemeral environments. Hands-on experience with Docker, Helm and a shared Kubernetes
cluster, plus Python and Bash tooling. Seeking to move into a DevOps or platform engineering role
full time.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw |
2021–Present
• Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams ( 25 developers), covering build, unit,
integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
• Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching
dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand ephemeral environments.
• Built ephemeral test environments for each merge request using Docker Compose, later adopting
Helm charts on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster.
• Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the
flaky-test rate from 7% to under 1%.
• Developed Bash and Python tooling to seed test data into PostgreSQL.
QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
• Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications for client projects.
• Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
• Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.
Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
• Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.
EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018
TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and Infrastructure: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Programming and Scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Systems and Monitoring: Linux, Git, PostgreSQL, Grafana (dashboards for test metrics)
LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role supporting Fleet
Connectivity. Over the past two years, my QA automation work has focused primarily on
CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. I am now looking to move into DevOps
or platform engineering full time, and I am drawn to this opportunity to help build
infrastructure for a new generation of connected trains.
At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines supporting three product teams and
approximately 25 developers. I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by
parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand
ephemeral environments. I built those environments with Docker Compose and later Helm
charts on a shared Kubernetes cluster. This work has given me practical experience improving
the reliability and operability of shared engineering systems used by three product teams, with
pipeline changes supporting approximately 25 developers.
I also maintain a pytest and Playwright suite of approximately 900 tests, reducing the flaky-test
rate from 7% to under 1%, and have developed Python and Bash tooling for PostgreSQL
test-data seeding. I have also used Linux and Grafana dashboards for test metrics,
strengthening my ability to troubleshoot systems and make reliability trends visible. Earlier, I
configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs and investigated customer issues using logs
and databases. I would bring this hands-on CI/CD, test-infrastructure, automation and
analytical experience to Corvale’s work on a reliable and observable train-to-cloud platform,
while continuing to develop across the role’s broader infrastructure responsibilities.
Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on end-to-end ownership make this role
especially compelling to me. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience
building and improving CI and test infrastructure could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity
team.
Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
